question: How many purchase-surface presentations, authoritative allowance reaches, visible blocks, upgrade intents, checkout opens, client success navigations, and real restores occur per namespace/build? The eight Subscription-prefixed events use closed dimensions only. Paywall Viewed is once per presentation, Upgrade Tapped is CTA intent, Checkout Opened requires an actual checkout page/window, and Checkout Completed is success navigation ONLY, never accepted payment, entitlement or revenue. Upgrade-in-place and reactivation are not checkout completion. Cancellation, dismissal and load/request failures never complete; entitlement refresh or focus cannot manufacture completion. An observed success navigation may precede entitlement-refresh lag. Web and external-browser chat checkout have no observable client completion signal; use authoritative server billing/invoice truth and its paid/trial classification. Billing Subscription Started is a lifecycle signal, not by itself proof of a charge. Restore is server refresh on Flutter only and must classify the fresh read/error, never stale paid state. Legacy Paywall Opened, Upgrade Plan Selected, Upgrade Succeeded and Upgrade Cancelled retain their prior behavior. Upgrade Modal Clicked/Dismissed are not purchase measurements. See contracts/analytics/PURCHASE_EXPOSURE.md for platform boundaries and limits.
zero_policy: Zero new events is expected before this client revision ships. Missing events are unobserved, not evidence of no exposure, cancellation, failed payment or no restore. Web/external-browser client completion and native store restore are unsupported where no corresponding signal/action exists. Revenue and paid conversion must use authoritative server billing records, not these client observations.
